1.explanation: Both HeaderMenu and SideNavMenu are exported by passing an anonymous function into React.forwardRef. Because that wrapper is unnamed and no displayName is assigned, React DevTools falls back to “Anonymous.” To fix this, after creating the forwarded component, assign its displayName property (e.g. ForwardedHeaderMenu.displayName = 'HeaderMenu') before exporting, so DevTools will show the proper component names.
1.bug_scenario: When inspecting the UIShell in React DevTools, both the header submenu (HeaderMenu) and the side-nav submenu (SideNavMenu) appear as “Anonymous” entries. This is because each of these subcomponents is exported via an anonymous React.forwardRef wrapper that has no displayName set, so DevTools cannot show their real names.

2.explanation: Both HeaderMenu and SideNavMenu are defined as React class components with the correct names, but at the bottom of each file they are re-exported via React.forwardRef(...) inline without assigning a displayName. React DevTools uses the displayName on forwardRef wrappers to show component names; without that, they render as “Anonymous.” To fix this bug, the forwardRef-wrapped exports need to be assigned displayName properties matching their underlying component names (e.g. ForwardRefHeaderMenu.displayName = 'HeaderMenu').
2.bug_scenario: When using the React DevTools Components panel to inspect the UIShell’s subcomponents, the menu elements created by HeaderMenu and SideNavMenu (which are exported via React.forwardRef) show up as “Anonymous” rather than their component names. In the screenshots you can see that both the header’s submenu and the side nav’s submenu wrappers appear with the label “Anonymous” in the component tree.
